Where it began

Suresh Raina was born in Muradnagar, in Uttar Pradesh, on 27 November 1986. In 1998 he moved to Lucknow to attend Guru Gobind Singh Sports College, and he soon rose to captain Uttar Pradesh's under-16 side.

He was picked for India Under-19s' tour of England at fifteen and a half, made his Ranji Trophy debut at 16, and at the 2004 Under-19 World Cup hit 90 from 38 balls. A Border–Gavaskar scholarship then took him to the Australian Cricket Academy.

The player

His one-day career began at Dambulla in 2005, but he had to wait five more years for his first Test. When it came, against Sri Lanka in July 2010, he made 120, becoming the 12th Indian to score a hundred on Test debut. He went on to become the first Indian to make a hundred in all three international formats.

In 18 Tests between 2010 and 2015 he made 768 runs at 26.48, with that hundred and seven fifties, and took 13 wickets with his off-spin. The white-ball game suited him best: he was part of the sides that won the 2011 World Cup and the 2013 Champions Trophy, and his unbeaten 34 alongside Yuvraj Singh helped India past Australia in the 2011 quarter-final.

What made him special

He was a joy to watch in the field. Quick, sharp and deadly with his throw, he patrolled the inner ring and ran batters out, and the former South African cricketer Jonty Rhodes put him at the top of his list of the best. With the bat he loved the leg side, flicking, pulling and slog-sweeping, and he made room to hit the ball inside out through the off side.

The short ball was never his favourite delivery, and bowlers knew it. He scored his runs all the same.

Away from the middle

He led India in one-day cricket, and in Bangladesh in 2014 his side defended a total of just 105 to win by 47 runs. With Chennai Super Kings he won four IPL titles and became the first batter to reach 5,000 IPL runs. On 15 August 2020 he said goodbye to international cricket only minutes after his captain and team-mate MS Dhoni had done the same. He later turned to commentary, and in 2023 opened an Indian restaurant in the Netherlands.

And finally

His best bowling in Tests was 2 for 1, which any spinner would frame. He also sang a song for the 2015 film Meeruthiya Gangsters, and in Galle in 2010 he and Harbhajan Singh recreated the famous pose from Titanic.
